concepts.why: Academic/secular and Baptist/Reformed/Lutheran readers: Col 2:11 does not say 'heart' (it says the putting off of the sinful nature, 'not by human hands'), so it shares the word 'circumcised' but not the concept the name states. Its next verse (2:12, baptism) is exactly where Baptist and Reformed/Lutheran/Catholic readers part on circumcision and baptism, so keeping 2:11 under a heart-circumcision name invites that reading without the text saying it. Rom 2:29 does say 'a matter of the heart' and stays.

Academic reader: Deut 31:26 says 'Book of the Law' beside 'the ark of the covenant', not 'the words of this covenant' or 'Book of the Covenant'; it does not say what the name says. It belongs with the ark (concept 9) and is already in the Witness secondary, so move it to concept 9 rather than lose it.

Academic reader: Ps 50:5 says 'made a covenant with Me by sacrifice' and says nothing of blood; the name ('The blood of the covenant', Exod 24:8, Zech 9:11, Matt 26:28, Heb 9:20) says more than this passage. Keep it under the Sacrifice link or the Sacrifice-related secondary, not under a blood concept.

Jewish-reader-of-the-Hebrew-Bible / academic / dispensational Baptist: 2 Cor 1:20 has neither the word 'covenant' nor any reference to the patriarchs; it says only that 'all the promises of God are Yes in Christ'. Set beside Gen 12 as the last item it reads as the site saying the Abrahamic promises are fulfilled in Christ, which is the claim the drafter rightly removed when it dropped 'Fulfillment in Christ'. Rom 15:8 names the patriarchs' promises and Rom 9:4, Acts 3:25, Gal 3:17 and Eph 2:12 all say 'covenant(s)', so they stay in their own words with no gloss. Gen 12:2-3, 7 carry the promise without the word 'covenant' (it first appears at 15:18); acceptable because Eph 2:12's name is the NT's own, but the name should not be taken to say Gen 12 is called a covenant.

note_fixes: Genesis 21:27-32: six verses where the concept needs less; trim to 21:27, 31-32 (the covenant, the oath, 'After they had made the covenant at Beersheba'); the lamb-and-well detail in 28-30 is not the concept.
concepts.why: Completeness of passage: none should be longer than the concept needs.

Academic and biblical-theological readers: Hos 2:18 is a covenant with the beasts, birds and creeping things and does not say betroth or marriage; it shares the word 'covenant' only. Give it a home in a covenant-with-creation concept (see missing) rather than under the marriage name. Hos 2:19-20, Ezek 16:8, Isa 54:5, Jer 31:32 stay.

Academic/secular and Jewish readers: Exod 32:19 says Moses threw the tablets and shattered them; it does not say a covenant was broken, so the passage supplies the reading and the name states it. If a tablets passage is wanted, Deut 9:15 and 9:17 (the 'two tablets of the covenant', then threw and smashed them) say the covenant word themselves; verify wording in the BSB before use. Otherwise let Deut 31:16, Judg 2:20, 2 Kgs 17:15 carry the concept.

Academic reader with the Hebrew in mind (the original arbitrates): the BSB at Neh 9:38 says 'a binding agreement' and at 10:29 'a sworn oath'; neither says 'covenant', and the name 'Made a covenant before the LORD' is built on 2 Kgs 23:3. A name that says more than two of its passages. If the Ezra-Nehemiah pledge is wanted it should sit under a name that fits what it says ('a binding agreement'); alternatively add the verses that do say 'made a covenant before the LORD', 2 Chronicles 34:31 and 2 Chronicles 23:16 (verify wording in the BSB). Catholic/Orthodox/Reformed readers will not miss the Nehemiah pair if Josiah's and Jehoiada's covenants stay.

Israel and the church, where Jewish, dispensational, Reformed, Catholic and Orthodox readers part. (a) Eph 2:19 has no covenant and no 'holding fast'; it says Gentiles are 'no longer strangers and foreigners' and does not say they are the foreigners of Isa 56:6. Putting it under a name taken from Isa 56:6 equates Gentile believers with those foreigners, which Jewish and dispensational readers read as the church replacing or joining Israel and Reformed/Catholic readers as the church as covenant people, with the text not saying so. Eph 2:12 already carries Ephesians in concept 21 in the text's own words. (b) Isa 49:8 says 'a covenant for the people' with no mention of foreigners or nations (49:6 would); Jewish readers take 'the people' there as Israel, so the grouping chooses a reading. Isa 42:6 stays because the same verse says 'a light to the nations'. Gen 17:12, Deut 29:11-12, Isa 56:6-7 stay.

secondary_or_links: Section C and the links: accept as is; the quotations are the verses and nothing names fulfilment. 'Covenant -> Priesthood' and 'Covenant -> Spirit' correctly stay as plain labels.

Concept 14 (1 Pet 2:9 beside Exod 19:5-6): kept, because the concept is a phrase and the name says nothing of who holds it; this is the Israel/church line and the page must never add a gloss to it. Same for 2 Cor 6:16 and Rev 21:3 in concept 13.

Concept 22: consider adding Joshua 9:15 ('made peace with them and made a covenant', the Gibeonites; verify wording in the BSB), which sets against concept 23 the covenant Israel did make with a people it was told to make none with. Suggested, not required.

Concept 30: Heb 8:13 ('first obsolete') and 2 Cor 3:14 ('old covenant') are deliberately absent and that is acceptable; if either is ever added it goes in with its verse as written and no concept may say the first covenant is replaced.
Hos 6:7 ('like Adam they broke the covenant') is rightly absent: the BSB and the Hebrew allow 'like Adam' or 'at Adam', and a Reformed reader's 'covenant with Adam' would take a side. Do not add.

missing.sub_theme: The words of the covenant in the land of Moab
missing.why: Deut 29:1 itself says this covenant is 'in addition to the covenant He had made with them at Horeb'. It has no concept of its own: Deut 29 is spread across concepts 7, 8, 11, 13, 19 and 28. A reader of Deuteronomy expects the Moab covenant named as its own sub-theme, and the Horeb/Sinai concept then keeps only the Horeb texts.

missing.sub_theme: My covenant with the day and the night
missing.why: The texts speak of a covenant with day and night and with the beasts, birds and stones, besides Noah's covenant with 'every living creature'. Jer 33:25 sits only inside concept 31 and Hos 2:18 loses its home when dropped from concept 24. Verify Job 5:23 in the BSB before use.

missing.sub_theme: This will be My covenant with them
missing.why: Romans 9:4 and Ephesians 2:12 are in the outline, but Romans 11:27, where Paul says 'My covenant with them', is the NT verse every reader on Israel and the covenants looks for, and leaving it out while keeping the other two tilts the Israel/church balance one way. Quote it in its own words under no interpretive name. Verify the BSB wording and whether Isa 27:9 uses the word covenant in the Berean text before listing it.

A classic covenant text that the outline has not touched: 'the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire'. It must go in as the verse alone with no identification of the messenger (Jewish, Christian and academic readers identify him differently), and not under 'A mediator' or 'A new covenant'.
